reviews.text: I have a lot of mixed feelings on this one. It has some moments that were sweet. The acting was great. I've actually seen this before and remembered liking it quite a bit. But this time, I struggled a bit. Largely because I never actually really liked Chris Gardner. Everything he was doing felt really selfish. He demanded his kid stay with him even though he knows he has no way to support his kid. And as a result him and his kid have to really struggle. And it's kind of all his fault. He has another option by allowing the kid to go with his mom to New York. So the movie just made me feel frustrated and kind of pissed off at Chris that he couldn't put his own ego aside to just do what's best for his kid. Now it didn't really make sense to me that the mom didn't fight harder. I just felt like I was missing part of the story. Turns out I was and quite a bit. In the true story, Chris cheated on his wife and got his mistress pregnant. She tried to take their son but he kind of assaulted her and was arrested for that. She does end to taking their kid to New York deciding not to press charges and then eventually ends to taking the kid back after a few months to live with his dad. Then after he becomes a broker he arranged for the kid to stay with her due to his long work hours. This feels like important info to leave out. Finding this out, it just feels like the movie wasn't honest with me. And I find that to be kind of gross to be honest. If I were to treat this as a fictional story, I might feel a bit different. Still didn't like Chris Gardner, but I at least would respect that he was at least able to eventually future things out. And that itself can be a inspirational story. So the story isn't a bad one. But I am mixed on the message. In the ending, while Will Smith is narrating, he says this moment of my life is called happiness. And I don't know how I feel about that. Because having a successful career is not equivalent to happiness. Happiness can be found without success in your career. I do get that if you have no money or resources at all, and your basic human needs aren't being met, it is going to be hard to actually be happy. But having a lot of money isn't really what makes one happy. And it just feels like this movie unintentionally sends the message that to be happy you need to find success in your career, and I don't really think that's true. Anyway, the movie isn't bad exactly. It has it's good elements. But I certainly do have many issues with the movie. Enough where I don't think I would call the movie good. 5/10

The Pursuit of Happyness ist der American Dream Film schlechthin. Man muss nur alles geben, hart arbeiten und daran glauben, dann wird der Erfolg schon kommen. Nun, natürlich ist da etwas dran, egal, wie man ansonsten zu diesem Denken steht. Das Problem dieses Films liegt für mich nicht in der Geschichte, die er erzählt, denn die ist nett gemeint und zusätzlich mit toller Musik unterlegt. Doch es wird vorausgesetzt, dass wir diesen Erfolg selbst miterleben. Dass wir am Ende mindestens so aufgeregt sind wie Chris, ob er den Job nun bekommt oder nicht. Es muss das Publikum emotional mitreißen. Und hier komme ich zu meinem Hauptproblem des Films: Das schafft er einfach nicht. Jedenfalls nicht bei mir. Aber man möge mir die Möglichkeit geben, mich zu erklären. Uns werden mehrere Situationen geschildert, die Chris immer wieder den Boden unter den Füßen wegziehen. Die Ehefrau verlässt ihren Mann und ihr Kind. Die Gläubiger stehen förmlich vor der Tür. Man verliert die Wohnung. Alles Situationen, in die man nicht gelangen möchte, da sie potenziell die eigene Existenz, beziehungsweise die der Familie bedrohen. Und während uns all das geschildert und gezeigt wird, geht The Pursuit of Happyness auf die wichtigsten Fragen, die sich aus dieser Konsequenz ergeben, nicht ein. Denn, was macht all das mit den Menschen? Was macht es mit einem, ständig unsicher zu sein, was als Nächstes passiert? Und wie reagiert man darauf? Diese Fragen ergeben sich gezwungenermaßen aus der Handlung. Doch darüber erfährt man kaum etwas. Dafür sind die Dialoge/ das Drehbuch insgesamt zu oberflächlich. Es werden hier und da schöne Worte gefunden, um die Botschaft des Films zu formulieren(was in den Szenen auch sinnvoll ist, nicht nur Exposition, was der Film aussagen möchte). Aber das Innere der Charaktere wird so gut wie gar nicht beleuchtet. Dadurch verliert der Film enorm viel an Gewicht, weil die emotionalen Szenen dann natürlich nicht so stark wirken können, wie sie sollten. Hinzu kommt, dass The Pursuit of Happyness quasi durchgängig optimistisch ist. Was ich auch per se nicht schlecht finde, allerdings war es dem Film in diesem Fall meiner Ansicht nach nicht zuträglich. Das passiert hauptsächlich durch die Musik und Kamera, die beide wirklich gut sind, aber ich hätte mir gewünscht, manchmal auch etwas kälter in der Inszenierung zu sein, da man dadurch eher Mitgefühl erzeugt hätte. Somit ist tolle Kameraarbeit, tolle Musik, gutes Schauspiel und eine eigentlich motivierende Botschaft in einem zu oberflächlichen Film gefangen und kann seine Wirkung nicht so wirklich entfalten.

Gabriele Muccino accomplishes a rare, difficult feat for a European director: flawlessly executing a quintessential American "rag-to-riches" story. While his broader filmography remains polarizing, The Pursuit of Happyness stands as a major production and editorial triumph.

Shockingly, this film came out before the late-00s financial crisis. It would have felt even more relevant a year or two later, when a LOT of people were feeling a money crunch. But its concerns are sadly evergreen. Times are really tough right now, and I feel that as a parent of three kids. When the film focuses on that, it’s very effective. I want to see a struggling father succeed for the sake of his son, of course. I am quite privileged, but I think about what I would do to provide for my family if the worst happened. The film loses me in the details, though. It feels like Chris is in this mess because of many boneheaded decisions made before and during the film that strain my sympathies. His wife leaves and he insists that she’s incapable of caring for their son. Why? I’ve seen no indication that she’s a poor mother. Am I supposed to read that as Chris’ pride or his understanding that his wife is a poor provider? And his big win is becoming a stockbroker, the kind of person who creates financial crises that will put more people in these conditions. A lot of these thoughts are front-loaded in the film for me. The ending pulls at the heartstrings just right and makes me feel the joy. But I found it a slog to get there. All that aside, the big takeaway here is Will Smith. It’s a great acting performance, it’s a better box office performance. Smith was the biggest movie star of the 00s. Whether it was action, sci-fi, a rom-com, an original superhero film, his films were successful. He could take this schmaltzy, manipulative pap and make it one of the top ten films of the year. His star power was off the charts, and that’s rewlly interesting to me. Watched as part of a 20th anniversary 2006 retrospective.
As Paige said “it was like watching someone have a bad day for 2hr.” The emotion was great, I was invested, but the only emotion was struggle for literally the whole film. Too much running.

Pull Yourself Up by Your Bootstraps: The Movie I get why people like, or even love this movie. It’s well made for the most part, and it boasts career best performances from both Will and Jaden Smith (not that that’s saying much in Jaden’s case, but I digress). But man, this is just straight up capitalist propaganda wrapped up in a feel good package. The movie unironically depicts Thomas Jefferson and Ronald fucking Reagan as inspirational figures! The message of this movie is essentially that you can work yourself out of poverty by working hard enough and being treated poorly by rich white guys. I understand that this is based on a true story, and that Chris Gardner actually did manage to work hard enough to get out of the dumps, but this movie isn’t interested in engaging with the class system that it relies on to get dramatic moments out of. On the contrary, it has the opposite of class consciousness in a way that hasn’t aged well in the slightest post-2008 financial crisis. I don’t hate this movie, but I hate its message and thematic content. It’s almost offensive to me, and it certainly insults my intelligence.

A melancholic watch, focusing on a beautiful father-son relationship, The Pursuit of Happyness goes onto show just how much money controls the quality of our lives. While Christopher’s character can be admired for his perseverance, grit, determination and for being a lovely father, the film glorifies the idea of “pulling yourself up from your bootstraps..” The film understands and in turn, portrays the phenomenology of poverty, struggle and sorrow without holding back. But what it fails to do is critique a system that is radically capitalistic, feeds upon ‘productivity culture’ and normalises kissing the ass of rich men just so you can ‘climb up the ladder.’ Success stories, like Christopher’s, will always be loved; they are inspiring. But one person’s success does not serve to acquit a system that constantly and deliberately keeps people on the brink of collapse and poverty.

Film del 2006, diretto da Gabriele Muccino. Chris Gardner viene lasciato dalla moglie e si ritrova ad affrontare enormi problemi economici, dovendo al tempo stesso prendersi cura del figlio piccolo Christopher. Questo film drammatico mi colpisce sempre molto personalmente. Nonostante presenti qualche limite dal punto di vista tecnico, la sceneggiatura, ispirata a eventi realmente accaduti, riesce sempre a coinvolgermi emotivamente. Narra la storia di un uomo che ha scommesso sull’investimento sbagliato e che si ritrova a dover far fronte a una serie di disavventure che si intrecciano con gravi problemi economici. Dallo sfratto all’abbandono da parte della moglie, passando per lo scarso profitto dei macchinari che cerca invano di vendere, Chris arriva a decidere di cambiare vita, trovando il coraggio e l’ambizione di intraprendere una nuova strada: uno stage non retribuito come broker. È commovente la dedizione, la passione e la resilienza di Chris, il quale, nonostante i numerosi problemi, continua imperterrito sulla propria strada, cercando di barcamenarsi tra il lavoro come venditore, la gestione del figlio e l’impegno dello stage, che prevede ore di studio ma anche l’acquisizione di nuovi clienti. Questo film ci ricorda quanto, anche nei momenti più bui, spesso ci si possa aggrappare a qualcosa, cercando di cambiare l’ordine degli addendi e, di conseguenza, il risultato della propria vita. Il coraggio di Chris, la sua abnegazione conciliata all’ambizione, hanno come propulsore principale la sofferenza, la povertà e l’incapacità di dare al proprio figlio ciò che desidera. E forse questo film, ripeto, nonostante presenti qualche pecca tecnica, mi colpisce sempre nel profondo, probabilmente proprio per le tematiche affrontate, che coincidono con un particolare periodo della mia vita. Questo lungometraggio, per quanto mi riguarda, è terapeutico: un film che, a ogni visione mi migliora l’umore e mi fa credere un po’ di più in me stesso. Per quanto concerne il comparto tecnico, la regia di Muccino prevede un utilizzo della macchina a mano che reputo disordinato e poco pulito. L’angolazione con cui viene posta la macchina da presa in alcune scene non mi convince, così come non mi convince appieno il blocking degli attori, in particolar modo nelle scene domestiche o in quelle racchiuse entro quattro mura. Risultano invece più azzeccate le scene all’aperto, ambientate in una New York movimentata, con Chris che inizialmente sembra andare quasi sempre nel verso opposto rispetto alla folla. Il film, invece, si conclude con un Chris perfettamente integrato in quella stessa folla, mentre cammina sui marciapiedi di New York. Gradisco questa rappresentazione di una New York frenetica e caotica. La macchina da presa si concentra spesso sulle lunghe file nei dormitori della Caritas, fotografando una parte della popolazione in difficoltà. Apprezzo l’intenzione di Muccino di mostrare anche questo volto della città, lontano dall’immagine patinata e idealizzata di New York. Will Smith è ottimo e riesce a essere estremamente coinvolgente dal punto di vista emotivo. Ottima anche la performance del giovane Jaden Smith. Voto: 8

Invalutabile (3 stelle messe come placeholder). La quintessenza di Muccino e se vogliamo l’inizio della sua fine in America. La scelta di vedere questo film (per altro iniziato alle 3 di notte) ha confermato le mie tendenze masochistiche recenti. Leggendo online ci trovo però dettagli che mi creano una sorta di “calore all’italiana”, cioè la vera storia di Gardner diversa, tutto un sottotesto personale tranciato di netto per farti empatizzare di più col personaggio. Tutto molto “familiare” insomma, con cose fatte magistralmente, cose fatte meno bene ed altre cose fatte ancora meglio ma per intortare lo spettatore. Se Muccino soffrisse all’epoca della direzione di questo film del complesso dell’impostore non lo so. So solo che Will Smith (ed Eva Mendes) ha fatto di tutto in questo film per farlo arrivare. Ma sarà arrivato?

A Classic American Dream Movie, But A Tone Deaf Film First I want to say I actually don’t dislike this film. I thought it was a good fun watch that was obviously made with lots of care and good intentions. The low lows we experience with Chris are trully devastating making it feel like your really there struggling alongside him. The amount of time and care the producers put into Chris’s personality and life make you really feel for him and see that he doesn’t deserve to be in this terrible situation. It has everything you would want in an American Dream™️ Movie. The zero to hero story, idealizing capitalism, and the ultimate message of work hard and you can achieve anything. But that’s not true. And this brings me to my main problem with this film. The Ideal (Fake) America Chris, the rest of his family and all the other characters, live in an ideal America free of racial or class bias that does not exist and has Never existed. This film focuses on the struggle of the working class black man in 1980s America but forgets about the fact he is working class and more importantly black. You really expect the audience to believe that in 1981 a rich millionaire CEO is inviting a black middle class intern with him to a football game in his private box because he just knocked on his door. Chris faces no sort of pressure or discrimination in this regard. Changing his race would have zero impact on the story. It seems Chris himself doesn’t even know he’s black. He is constantly quoting Thomas Jefferson a known racist and proud slave owner, and watching Ronald Reagan on the tv (No idea what that scene added). The film also glamorizes Chris bringing his son with him into homeless because he’s “In the pursuit of happiness” and it’s all gonna work out. While simultaneously shaming his wife for wanting to take her son away to a better place Final Notes It’s still a good movie overall aside from all these complaints. Will smith did a great job as Chris and Jayden was phenomenal. To think he was only around 7 years old when this was filmed is insane.

для меня очень противоречивый фильм. вроде есть и такая тихая грусть и светлая радость за финал, но сколько же есть НО 1. на мой вкус, Кристофер абсолютный бытовой инвалид. в вашей семье оба надрывают спины, чтобы хоть как-то закрыть долги, а ты не можешь за собой тарелку помыть…меня это оч вынесло, причем это +- самое начало 2. такое больно говорить, но если вы всю жизнь сводите концы с концами, то вам не нужен ребенок. за весь фильм мне больше всех было жалко именно его. в начале была фраза о том, что Кристофер хотел, чтобы его ребенок знал, что такое иметь отца, чтобы его судьба отличалась от судьбы его ребенка. но как итог, это были бесконечные мытарства по ночлежкам, мотелям и прочему. конечно, нужно принимать во внимание, что они думали, что их обогатят продажи этих херовин, но нельзя ставить все ставки на одну ячейку в рулетке. спасибо, что все в итоге закончилось позитивно, но какого-то чувства облегчения это не принесло 3. мне кажется правильным, что линию Линды больше не показали. она просто устала от груза, который приходилось нести ей. спасибо, что никто хоть не додумался себя убить короче, очень много пассивного гнева меня заставил испытать этот фильм. сдерживал его только коллективный просмотр в незнакомой компании
